summary: George Bidie worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Marischal College, Aberdeen (M.D. ~1849–1853) and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Professor of Botany at Madras Medical College (1866–1870) and Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (1872–1884).
George Bogle was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He was educated at Enfield Academy and studied at the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1760 to 1764.

George Bosworth Burch worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Harvard, Geneva, and Paris. He taught as Professor of philosophy and psychology at the College of Idaho (1942–1946) and Fletcher Professor of Philosophy at Tufts University (1946–1967).
George Byres Mainwaring was an Indologist and linguist. He served in the Bengal Army as an ensign from 1842 and attained the rank of Lieutenant-Colonel in the Bengal Staff Corps in 1868.

George C. O. Haas was an Indologist who earned his A.B. and Ph.D. under A. V. Williams Jackson at Columbia University. He taught German at City College of New York (1904–1916) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1917–1920).

George Campbell was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He was educated at Edinburgh Academy, Madras College, Hamilton Academy, the University of St Andrews, East India Company College, and the University of Oxford (D.C.L. 1874).

George Cardona worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at NYU, Yale (MA), with traditional Indian scholars, and under Warren Cowgill and Paul Thieme. He was a longtime Professor of Linguistics at the University of Pennsylvania (~1965–2006).
George Carstairs worked in religious studies and Indology. He was educated at The Albany Academy and studied at the University of Glasgow, where he earned an M.A. (~1897–1901) and a D.D. (~1935).

George Chatalian was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at Brown University and Harvard University (Ph.D. 1968). He taught at Franklin Pierce University, the University of Lagos, and Obafemi Awolowo University (1983).

George Chemparathy is an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Paul Hacker and completed his doctorate under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna (~1959–1963). He served as a professor at Utrecht University (~1971–1990).

George Christopher Molesworth Birdwood worked in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at the University of Edinburgh (M.D. ~1849–1854), he was a professor at Grant Medical College (~1858–1868) and a Special Assistant at the India Office (1878–1899).

George Cowgill was an archaeologist who studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Harvard University (~1956–1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1960–1990) and Arizona State University (~1990–2018).

George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London (~1861–1863). He served on the faculty at University College London from approximately 1866 to 1892.

George Cœdès was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at EPHE, Berlin, and EFEO. He served as Director of EFEO (1929–1947), Conservator of the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929), and President of the Société Asiatique (1965–1969).

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD at Northwestern University (~1968–1972), where he later served as Professor of Religion (~1974–2014).

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).
George Ernest Ward was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his education in Oxford, studying at The Queen's College (~1856–1858) and Wadham College (~1858–1860, M.A.).

George Eugene Dunkel is a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Karl Hoffmann and at the University of Pennsylvania (~1970–1976). He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Princeton, and the University of Zurich, taking the Indo-European chair in 1986.

George Everest worked in Indology and related technical fields. Educated at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1804–1806), he joined the Great Trigonometrical Survey in 1817 and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India (1830–1843).

George F. Dales was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania (~1953–1960), he held posts at Penn and became Professor of Near Eastern and South Asian Archaeology at UC Berkeley in 1972.
